name: Kaguare, el oso melero

paletteRoles.ink: every outline (body and head 3, limbs and tail 2.8, the open paws 2.6, the brooch ring 2.2, the claws 1.1), the nose pad, the pupils, the "o" mouth, inner lines 2.0–2.2
paletteRoles.fur: head, neck and throat, limbs, hindquarters, tail, the open palms
paletteRoles.furShade: the far limbs behind the body, the inside of the ear
paletteRoles.vest: the black vest, a warm near-black: 9.43:1 against the fur, so it reads black at 48 px. It runs right to the outline (no fur rim), so the silhouette edge is the ink outline on the background; also the tail blotches
paletteRoles.eyeRing: the narrow ring round the small dark eye
paletteRoles.claw: the short rounded claws and the palm pads
paletteRoles.cheek: the cheek blush and the pink of the open smile
paletteRoles.tajyPink: the notebook ribbon, the stand-in rosette, the icon tile
paletteRoles.sweat: the sweat drop (the games' own drop colour)
paletteRoles.white: the brooch disc, the notebook pages, the eye glint
paletteRoles.appGround: the app's ground (#F4F5F9), checked on the sheet

standing.notes: Main pose: Goal 104 px, Main and Progress 60, the hints 48, results 72, Escribir at 90 % and Hablar at 75 %. Side view facing right on all fours; the near legs only, so squash, stretch, the spin and the hop read as one sticker. Feet on y 83: the soles are flat on y 83 and their outline ends at y 84.5; painted bounds x 2.3–95.1, y 25.2–84.5, stroke included; centre of mass x 49.5. Outline top y 25.2 at the ear (x 61.8–62.4); the back's outline top at x 50 is y 40.8; the crown, the top of the head itself clear of the ear, is y 30.9 at x 70 (the umbrella stick ends there); the snout tip is at (95.1, 56.4), and no card may reach it (see the games). With the sweat drop and the sparks showing, the art reaches y 17.2 and x 99.3. The head: a round cranium with the round ear set at the back, the small dark eye in a narrow ring, then a stop in front of the eye and the tube snout, nearly one depth to a blunt, slightly down-curved tip; the head is carried a little low, nose forward, as a walking tamandua carries it. The black vest covers the withers right up to the back of the head, runs over the shoulder and round the root of the near foreleg to the belly, and its rear edge sweeps back to the hip, so the hindquarters stay pale; a small pale bib shows under the throat. The foreleg is a separate shape whose round top sits inside the vest (the armhole); two short cream claws sit at the front of the forefoot. Brooch on the vest at (45,60.2).

fallen.notes: Knocked over by a word card: on its back on the ground line (y 83), the near forepaw up and flopped over with its three cream claws turned down, the hind foot up and back toward the tail, the head resting on its jaw at the right with a spiral (dazed) eye and a small ink "o" mouth inside the head at the base of the snout; no X eyes, no tears, never hurt. Painted bounds x 2.1–98.6, y 33.2–84.5: 49.8 units tall (top at the forepaw, y 33.2), under the 62 the games allow, so the orbiting stars fit above it. Its mass sits over the standing pose's (centre x 46.5 against 49.5) and its brooch at (40.2,65.6) is 7.2 units from the standing one, so the two crossfade in place. The snout tip is at (98.6, 76.9). The games may tilt this layer up to ±8° or squash it (1.14 / 0.86) about 50 % 83 %.

rising.notes: Opu'ã · Se levantó, the brand's key moment, and the middle step of every fall in the games (fallen → rising → standing). The tamandua's tripod made friendly and proud: up on its hind legs, the tail planted long and diagonal behind as the third leg, both arms raised about 25° above level with the paws open, pale palms to the viewer and three short cream claws on each (a "ta-da", never the level-armed defensive stand), chin up, open eye and smile. The belly ends at y 76.2, so about 4 units of pale hind leg (as under the standing pose) and the whole foot show below its outline (the soles flat on y 83, toes forward; the legs are painted behind the body, as in the standing pose). The vest covers the trunk from the back of the neck and the shoulders down the back and under the belly, so both arms leave it like arms from armholes; the throat, a narrow bib in front and a rounded thigh at the front hip stay pale. Feet on y 83; painted bounds x 2.8–92.1, y 16.3–84.4; centre x 48.4. The brand card's stamp corner (x 0–18, y 0–21) is empty (0 painted pixels).

cheering.notes: ¡Vy'apavẽ! · ¡Felicitaciones!: the same upright body (the hind legs and feet showing below the belly, the pale thigh at the front hip), the head thrown back, happy (arc) eyes, the open smile (pink above an ink smile arc, inside the head), both arms up with open paws, the tail swung up in a curl, three gold sparks #F2B43A. On the brand board it carries the "whole" rosette. Feet on y 83; painted bounds x 14.5–98.9, y 6.5–84.4 (the animal alone reaches y 8.8; the sparks reach y 6.5).

studying.notes: Mbo'epy · Lección: the standing body (same feet, same brooch, the vest up over the withers to the head) with the head lowered over an open notebook on the ground in front of it: white pages, ink outline 2.6, two grey lines a page, a spine, and a pink #C2336F ribbon that ends at y 85. The eye looks down at the page and the snout tip stays clear of it (reading, not touching). Painted bounds x 2.3–98.3, y 31.4–85.

oops.notes: Eha'ã jey · Intentá de nuevo: a gentle mistake (Teach, Compare and Build at 48 px, results at 72). Sitting back on its haunches with the tail on the ground, the near paw resting on its lower cheek behind the mouth, its claws curled against the cheek so only the round back of the paw shows; sheepish closed happy eyes, a small smile and a sweat drop #9FD3F5. The paw keeps 3 units of fur between it and the eye and stays clear of the mouth and the snout (no paw on the nose), so the face does not clump at 48 px; no tears, never sad. The pale forearm crosses the dark vest, so the gesture still reads at 40–48 px. The vest runs from the nape (over the withers) down the back to the hip; the rump, the folded hind leg and a bib under the throat stay pale. Seated: the rump and the hind foot rest on y 83. Painted bounds x 2.7–93.3, y 10.8–84.8.

icon-pink.notes: App icon on tajy pink #C2336F: rect 100×100 rx 22.3, full bleed, no border of its own. Kaguare's head and shoulders, big: the round ear, the small dark eye in its ring, the cheek, the tube snout with its nose pad, and the black vest over the shoulders (right to the 4.4 outline, no fur rim) carrying the brooch with the complete rosette (the engine's "whole" sample nested at translate(36.4 85.8) scale(0.36) in an r 9.4 disc). The bust rises from the bottom edge: its back line meets it at x 24.8, past the rounded corner (which ends at x 22.3), so all four corners stay tile colour and the rounded square keeps its shape on a dark wallpaper at 29–40 px. The ink outline and the hard ink offset shadow (3.4, 3.4) belong to the mascot, as on the old icon. No clipPath: the bust and its shadow close straight along the bottom edge and the outline meets it at right angles with butt caps; a transparent render shows nothing outside the rounded square beyond antialiasing. Carries xmlns, so the same file is the 1024 master. Reads at 29 and 40 px.

icon-green.notes: The same icon on yerba green #2F7A35.

fallen-mini.notes: A simplified fallen pose for the games' "Caídas" counter (20 px, in Escribir and Hablar) and the mistake notebook (36 px, Review): heavy 5-unit outlines, two short bent paws up, the head (the same tube snout) resting at the right with a spiral eye, the dark vest with the white brooch (spokes and hub only, no ring, so it cannot read as a target); the tail keeps fur inside its outline right to the tip. It is decorative wherever it appears (the pill and the notebook entry carry their own text), so the SVG is aria-hidden="true", with no role or label, as the old ball was. Painted bounds x 2.2–98.3, y 27.5–84.5; it is a symbol, not placed on a ground line. At 20 px on a 1× screen it is a small figure; from 2× it reads as one lying on its back.

faceParts: Only the standing SVG carries switchable parts, and they are marked with data-part, never with ids, so any number of copies can share a page (the Goal, Drill and brand boards each show several). Inside its head group: <g data-part="eye-open"> (the small dark eye and its glint), <g data-part="eye-closed"> (the blink, a gentle downward arc), <g data-part="eye-happy"> (an upward arc ^), <g data-part="mouth-normal"> (a small ink smile at the base of the snout, under the cheek), <g data-part="mouth-o"> (a small ink "o", for worried or surprised) and <g data-part="mouth-happy"> (the open smile: pink above an ink smile arc); at the top level <g data-part="sweat"> (a drop #9FD3F5 above the forehead) and <g data-part="sparks"> (three gold strokes #F2B43A above the snout). As shipped, eye-open and mouth-normal show and the other six carry opacity="0". Show exactly one eye and one mouth at a time by opacity (1 on the one you want, 0 on its siblings); sweat and sparks are overlays on any face and stay clear of the head and of each other. The three eyes share one centre (head space 2.4, -2.4) and the three mouths one spot at the base of the snout, so switching never moves the face. Every mouth lies inside the head outline, with at least 0.4 units of fur between its ink and the ink of the jaw line (check-face.js), so none can read as a tongue. Always on: the eye ring, the cheek blush and the dark nose pad inside the snout tip. Bindings for the games, set on the groups themselves (as in opacity="{{ tat.eyeO }}"): eye-open ← eyeO, eye-closed ← blinkO, eye-happy ← happyO, mouth-normal ← mouthO, mouth-o ← ohO, mouth-happy ← (p.mouth === 'happy'), sweat ← sweatO, sparks ← sparkO; a script can also select them as [data-part="eye-open"]. Today happyO drives both the happy eye and the happy mouth, so a happy eye with the "o" mouth (worried during a streak) would show two mouths: give mouth-happy its own binding. The fixed poses draw their own faces and carry no data-part: rising (open eye, smile), cheering (happy eye, open smile), studying (eye looking down), oops (happy closed eye, small smile), fallen (spiral eye, small ink o).

stampCorner.region: drawing x 0–18, y 0–21 (the brand card puts its stamp there)

escribir: MASCOT = 0.9, FEET = 83. REACH = 50: at 90 % the standing snout tip (x 95.1) sits 40.6 px right of the centre and the fallen one (x 98.6) 43.7 px, so a card that reaches him makes him fall about 6 px before it could touch the snout.
The fallen ('down') layer sits at GROUND − FEET·MASCOT like the standing one, with transform-origin 50% 83% and a tilt of at most 8° (downRot = −8·k).
Stars: the orbit at GROUND − 70 (bottom edge GROUND − 55) clears the fallen pose, whose top is at GROUND − 44.8.

The fall: FADE_T = 0.1 (each crossfade) and UP_T = 0.3 (how long the rising pose shows): standing → fallen while dizzy, then fallen → rising (¡Opu'ã!), then rising → standing with the springy squash and stretch and the small hop; the fall's total length is unchanged. The rising layer shares the standing layer's left and top.

Tricks: jump and spin rise to 104 and 110 px so the snout clears the card passing under him; the smash is a stomp in place, so the snout never strikes the card; a passed card's stamp lands 72 px behind him (NODE_BACK), clear of his tail.
hablar: MASCOT = 0.75. YH = 43 ((83 − 25.2) × 0.75): cards land on the top of his head and his back, never on the snout, which is 31.2 units lower than the ear.
DOWN_TOP = 66·MASCOT: it must not go below 60·MASCOT, or the stars (their lowest edge is 7.5 px under the orbit's centre) touch the raised paw (the fallen pose reaches y 33.2).

The fallen layer sits at p.base − p.lift − FEET·MASCOT with transform-origin 50% 83%, so its 1.14/0.86 squash keeps his back on the ground; it fades in over 0.1 s and keeps its squash while it fades out.
Dodge: a sidestep and a lean (p.x += 46·out; p.rot = −0.12·out); the fallen layer never shows.
Umbrella: the stick ends on the crown at drawing x 70 (left = W / 2 + 15), drawn before the mascot layers so it runs behind Kaguare and his head hides its tip.
The fall: fallen → rising (UP_T = 0.3) → standing, as in Escribir; the climb keeps the standing layer.
mouth-happy is bound to p.mouth === 'happy' in both games.
The two 'Cómo jugar' cards use scenes.pick and scenes.compare.
boards: Rosette: on every brooch the boards nest C.rosette() as <g transform="translate(cx cy) scale(s)"> right after the disc circle, in place of the stand-in group <g class="rosette">…</g>: s 0.42 on every body pose, 0.36 in the icon. The engine's widest state, "whole", reaches r 21.96 in its own box (its scalloped rim; the other states reach r 20.0): 9.22 at 0.42, inside the body discs' inner edge (9.4), and 7.91 at 0.36, inside the icon disc's (8.0).
Brand board: the cards keep viewBox 0 0 125 112 with the drawing at translate(11 10); every brand pose leaves the stamp corner empty.
The "Caídas" pills (Escribir line 44, Hablar line 146) and the notebook (Review line 148): the fallen-mini SVG, which is aria-hidden (the pill and the entry carry the text).

rules: Name: Kaguare (with K, no accent, no diminutive); in Spanish "el oso melero". Labels read "Kaguare, el oso melero". Never "Kaguare'i", "Caguaré" or "perezoso". No etymology in the app.

Snout: short-to-moderate, a tube (a stop in front of the eye, then nearly one depth to a blunt, slightly down-curved tip), in the colour of the face to the tip, with only a small dark nose pad inside the tip. Never the punchline: no nose-bonks, no cards hitting the nose, no paw on the nose, no long-nose gags.

Tongue: none. Every mouth sits at the base of the snout, inside the head outline; no pink at or past the snout tip and none below the jaw line (the open smile's pink lies above its ink smile arc; the "o" is ink).
Not a pet: no collar, leash or kennel, no human carrying or cuddling it, no sweets or honey.
No menace: claws short and rounded (cream nubs, thinly outlined), never slashing; the rising stance is proud and open (arms raised, palms out), not a threat display.

The right species: pale golden fur, a black vest over the withers and the trunk (the forelegs come out of it like arms from armholes), round upright ears, a small dark eye, a long tapering prehensile tail, pale with a few irregular dark blotches (never bushy, never leopard spots), and no grey with a narrow diagonal shoulder stripe (the jurumi).
No smell gags, road jokes, Indigenous costume, feathers or headdresses.
Keep: the vest, the round ears, the small dark eye, the pale face and limbs, the prehensile tail, the tripod for "Opu'ã · Se levantó", and the ñandutí pinned on the vest like a brooch.
construction: viewBox 0 0 100 100 for every pose; flat fills, no gradients, masks, clipPaths or defs, and no ids at all (the standing pose's eight switchable parts are data-part attributes), so every pose and both icons can be pasted many times on one board. Ink outline 3 on the body and head, 2.8 on limbs and tail, 2.6 on the notebook and the open paws, 2.2 on the brooch ring, 2.0–2.2 for inner lines, 1.1 on the claws, round joins. The head and body are one silhouette: the head's outline is open from the nape to the throat, and the body's outline is stroked only where it shows (from the throat round the chest, belly and back to the nape), so there is no seam and no spike at the neck; the ear's base sits inside the head. The vest is painted between the body fill and the body outline and runs right to the outline, with no fur rim: near-black against the pale fur, with the ink outline as the silhouette edge. The claws are cream nubs at least 3 units wide with a 1.1 outline, painted over the paw, so they read as pale claws at 104–160 px. Every pose was checked with its strokes: all paint stays inside 0..100.
